title: Security posture discovery with Oakridge Capital
next_steps: Maya to share SOC 2 and ISO 27001 attestation notes and security whitepaper (link)
Jared to prepare Dedicated vs Hosted latency/cost spreadsheet and quantization/instance suggestions
Schedule technical deep dive with Oakridge infra team week of Mar 30 to run benchmark tests on sample workload
action_items: Maya Patel: Send SOC2 summary, ISO cert scan, and security whitepaper (due 2026-03-28)
Jared Kim: Build latency/cost comparison for hosted vs dedicated and example config for VPC/private deployment (due 2026-03-30)
Laura Chen (Oakridge): Share current data retention policy and architecture diagram showing where PII resides (due 2026-03-29)
meeting_header: Date: 2026-03-27 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jared Kim (Redwood SE), Samantha Brooks (Oakridge CTO), Ravi Menon (Oakridge Head Infra), Laura Chen (Oakridge Compliance)
summary: Discovery focused on Oakridge's security requirements for evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Key topics: SOC 2 / ISO attestation, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logging, encryption (KMS/HSM), data residency and retention. Oakridge favors dedicated or private due to compliance but wants to understand tradeoffs. Next steps: share security docs, schedule deep-dive and run benchmarks.
topics: SOC 2 and ISO 27001 attestation and scope
SSO/SAML and SCIM for user provisioning
Audit logs and retention/forwarding to SIEM
Encryption at rest and in transit, KMS/HSM integration
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
questions: Is Redwood SOC 2 Type II scoped for hosted and dedicated?
Can we integrate Oakridge KMS/HSM for key management in private deployments?
How does Redwood expose audit logs and can they be forwarded to our Splunk/Datadog?
What are the default retention windows and can they be customized per customer?
Does RBAC let us separate tenant admins from Redwood support?
transcript: [00:00] Maya Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intros?
[00:06] Samantha Brooks: Samantha Brooks, CTO at Oakridge. We run a mix of quant strategies and we need to be really careful about data custody and compliance.
[00:12] Ravi Menon: Ravi, infra. we're evaluating whether to use Redwood hosted for speed or move to dedicated/private for isolation.
[00:18] Laura Chen: Laura, compliance. my focus is SOC2, ISO, retention, auditability.
[00:25] Maya Patel: Great thanks. Jared from our infra team will cover technical bits. Jared?
[00:29] Jared Kim: Hey all. quick agenda: SOC2/ISO scope, auth (SSO/SAML/SCIM), RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, and data residency/retention. then Q&A and next steps.
[00:40] Samantha Brooks: speed matters but we're not willing to compromise on controls. do you have SOC2?

[00:45] Maya Patel: yes, Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and we're in the process of updating our ISO 27001 material; i'll send the attestation docs after the call. for hosted, SOC2 covers the hosted control plane and dataplane we operate. for Dedicated and Private we can provide additional contractual controls.
[00:59] Laura Chen: is the SOC2 scope the same for Dedicated? our legal wants explicit language about data segregation.

[01:05] Maya Patel: good question. dedicated pools are logically isolated and we include that in our SOC2 description, but for contractual guarantees we recommend dedicated contracts and addendums. we can also do a tailored statement for private/on-prem.
[01:18] Ravi Menon: what about ISO? we need ISO for some of our partners.
[01:22] Maya Patel: we're progressing on ISO 27001; we have the core policies and controls in place and can share the current certification timeline and scope. i'll include that in the doc packet.
[01:32] Samantha Brooks: SSO is critical. we run Okta. how does Redwood integrate?
[01:36] Jared Kim: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. most customers use Okta or Azure AD. there's also RBAC at the org/team level so you can restrict access—admins, devs, read-only, etc.
[01:48] Samantha Brooks: can we restrict Redwood support access? we don't want them accessing production prompts or logs.

[01:53] Jared Kim: absolutely. support access is role-based and can be limited; we also have audit logs for all console actions and API keys. for private deployments you can entirely manage keys and we can gate Redwood support via ticketed temporary access and approval workflows.
[02:05] Laura Chen: audit logs—what's included, retention, and forwarding options?

[02:09] Jared Kim: logs include auth events, admin actions, model served, request metadata (not full input by default in hosted but you can opt-in). retention defaults to 90 days for hosted but can be extended. logs can be streamed to your SIEM — we support forwarding to Splunk, Datadog, or S3 buckets. note: in some places the transcripting may show as 'audit log' or 'aud-it' in export, sorry that was my mic —
[02:30] Samantha Brooks: we need full request traceability for PII investigations. can we get request payloads in logs?

[02:35] Jared Kim: yes, with caveats. by default for privacy, hosted masks or redacts certain fields unless you opt in. for dedicated/private we can configure full payload logging into your secure storage. for hosted we offer tokenization and redaction tooling plus a configurable retention window.
[02:48] Ravi Menon: encryption — do you support customer-managed keys?

[02:52] Maya Patel: short answer yes for Private — you can bring your own KMS. For Dedicated we have a managed KMS but we can integrate customer KMS in many cases; for hosted we use our KMS but the keys are in a Redwood-controlled KMS. if you need HSM-backed keys we can discuss private or on-prem and KMS/HSM integrations.
[03:07] Laura Chen: is data encrypted in transit and at rest across all deployment modes?

[03:11] Jared Kim: yes, TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest. for additional compliance we can provide proof of encryption controls in the packet i share. if you require HSM-wrapped keys we recommend private deployment.
[03:22] Samantha Brooks: what about data residency — our bank partners require EU-only processing for certain datasets.

[03:27] Maya Patel: Redwood routes requests by region. Hosted has region-specific endpoints and we can ensure processing in eu-west or us-east based on tenancy. Dedicated and Private give stronger guarantees — you can pin capacity to a region or run on-prem in an EU datacenter.
[03:39] Ravi Menon: latency/cost tradeoff — we've seen big differences when we self-host. how do you recommend?

[03:44] Jared Kim: typically hosted for quick time-to-value and scale, dedicated for predictable throughput and isolation, private for strict regulatory needs. we have an Optimize toolkit to suggest batching/quantization combos to hit latency/cost targets. i'll prepare a spreadsheet showing token cost and latency for your sample prompt set.
[03:58] Samantha Brooks: about SAML — sometimes provisioning is flaky; do you provide SCIM and group sync?
[04:03] Jared Kim: yes SCIM provisioning is supported; group sync and mapping to RBAC roles is straightforward. i can share an Okta playbook we use with customers.
[04:12] Laura Chen: auditability again — can we get immutable logs and export them for audits?
[04:16] Maya Patel: yes we can provide immutable exports to S3 with object locks or send to your SIEM. we also support long-term retention add-ons.
[04:25] Samantha Brooks: legal will ask about subprocessor lists and network diagrams.
[04:29] Maya Patel: we'll include our subprocessor list and a high-level network/dataflow diagram. also i'll share the standard DPA and onboarding checklist.
[04:36] Ravi Menon: one more on RBAC — can we have separate orgs for dev vs prod and separate billing?
[04:40] Jared Kim: yes you can create multiple orgs or use projects/environments with strict separation; billing can be consolidated or split depending on contract.
[04:47] Samantha Brooks: if we start with hosted to evaluate, can we later move to dedicated without changing code?

[04:52] Maya Patel: that's a common question — you can pin model versions and keep API surface the same; migration is mostly a config and routing update. for some private/on-prem specifics there may be small networking changes but SDKs and endpoints remain consistent.
[05:02] Laura Chen: on retention, what's the default for embeddings and request logs? we need 7 years for some records.

[05:08] Jared Kim: default short-term retention is 90 days for request logs and embeddings retention is 30 days by default in hosted; Dedicated/Private can be configured to meet longer legal obligations like 7 years, but that affects storage cost — we'll surface that in the spreadsheet.
[05:20] Samantha Brooks: any penalties or compliance things for e-discovery?
[05:24] Maya Patel: we support e-discovery exports; for legal holds we can extend retention and provide exports. we'll add that to the legal packet.
[05:30] Ravi Menon: are there any known limitations with private deployments and model updates? e.g., lag to get latest model kernels or optimizations?

[05:36] Jared Kim: Private/on-prem has a deployment cadence agreed in the contract — patching and model upgrades can be scheduled. we provide backport patches for critical security issues. Dedicated gets faster rollout via our managed channels.
[05:48] Samantha Brooks: what about penetration testing and third-party audits?
[05:52] Maya Patel: we do annual pentests and third-party audits; we'll include summaries and scope. customers can also arrange on-site assessments for Private with appropriate NDAs.
[06:02] Laura Chen: ok. what will you send after this call?

[06:06] Maya Patel: SOC2 Type II report summary, ISO timeline, subprocessor list, DPA template, network diagrams, and a link to our Okta/SCIM playbook, plus Jared's latency/cost spreadsheet. also a link to our security whitepaper: https://redwood.ai/security-whitepaper.pdf
[06:20] Samantha Brooks: that sounds good. can we schedule the technical deep dive with infra folks next week?
[06:24] Maya Patel: yes i'll propose times — looking at Mar 30 or 31. Jared will lead the benchmark run.
[06:30] Ravi Menon: note: we'll need a non-prod test tenant that mirrors production network egress restrictions for the benchmark.
[06:35] Jared Kim: we can provision a dedicated test pool in the region you want and configure VPC egress. will include that in the plan.
[06:41] Samantha Brooks: pricing — high level now is fine, detailed later tied to dedicated capacity and retention costs.
[06:48] Maya Patel: we'll send an initial pricing estimate and then a formal quote once you pick dedicated vs private and retention options.
[06:54] Laura Chen: any red flags from a compliance standpoint we should be aware of?
[06:58] Jared Kim: nothing major; most concerns are configurable: key management, log retention, region pinning. private deployments require more ops upfront but give the control you need.
[07:08] Samantha Brooks: ok thanks all. quick recap?

[07:10] Maya Patel: recap: Redwood to share SOC2/ISO docs, subprocessor list, DPA, Okta playbook, network diagram, security whitepaper link, and Jared's latency/cost spreadsheet. schedule tech deep dive week of Mar 30 and Oakridge to share retention policy and architecture diagram. action owners and due dates noted in the follow-up.
[07:28] Samantha Brooks: thanks, appreciate it.
[07:30] Maya Patel: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs. bye.
[52:00] (call ended)
